response.why: Playing an untapped land (Island or Riverpyre Verge) sets up exactly 5 mana next window to hard-cast Eddymurk Crab as my first real threat/blocker, which is far more valuable than wasting Torch the Tower on a 4/5 it can't kill or skipping the land drop entirely to cast Glacial Dragonhunt (which even got Spell-Snared in one sample). Steam Vents-tapped and Spirebluff Canal don't provide the 5th mana this turn so they fail to enable Crab, and paying 2 life for Steam Vents is needless when free untapped lands are already in hand.
response.plan: Play Island (or Riverpyre Verge) this window, then hard-cast Eddymurk Crab as my first creature — a 5/5 body to finally contest the board and block Hearth Elemental. Keep both Torch the Tower copies for a creature they can actually kill.

response.why: With 5 mana available, hard-casting Eddymurk Crab now gives an untapped 5/5 body that can actually block their Hearth Elemental next turn (flashing it in reactively later would enter tapped and useless as a blocker), so it clearly beats Harmonize/Glacial Dragonhunt (more cards but still zero board presence against their growing threats) and especially Torch the Tower (wastes removal on a 4/5 it can't kill, sometimes even twice).
response.plan: Cast Eddymurk Crab now with no target (tapping their Hearth Elemental achieves nothing since it untaps normally on their turn) to finally get a real body on board. Keep both Torch the Tower copies for a smaller creature.

response.why: Hard-casting Hearth Elemental gives a second real body (4/5) without tapping my existing Eddymurk Crab, doubling my board while keeping the Crab up as a blocker — clearly the strongest play now that I have the mana. Torch the Tower still can't kill anything (all 5-toughness targets), Stoke Genius discards my whole hand of removal for only 2 cards (terrible), and Harmonize's tap-reduction leaves my only blocker tapped going into their turn.
response.plan: Cast Hearth Elemental as a hard-cast creature this turn to build a two-creature board (Eddymurk Crab + Hearth Elemental) while keeping the Crab untapped to block. Still hold both Torch the Tower copies for a smaller creature, and play a land if the window allows.

response.why: With Eddymurk Crab and Hearth Elemental both untapped as blockers, playing Riverpyre Verge (free, untapped, flexible R/U) develops for no downside; Spirebluff Canal/Steam Vents give no mana benefit this turn (tapped or costs life needlessly) and Harmonize taps one of my two blockers right when I need both up against their board. Torch the Tower still can't kill anything at 5 toughness, so using it wastes the card.
response.plan: Play Riverpyre Verge and pass otherwise, keeping both creatures untapped as blockers. Hold both Torch the Tower copies for a smaller creature.

request.aggregation: candidate value = mean over samples of its best leaf within each sample

response.why: Board favors me: three untapped creatures (Eddymurk Crab 5/5, Hearth Elemental 4/5, Sunderflock 5/5) against their weaker positioned board (one tapped, one summoning-sick, one live 5/5), so passing or drawing cards with Glacial Dragonhunt while staying fully back as blockers scores highest. Torch the Tower can't kill anything at 4-5 toughness on their side, so casting it for no kill scores well below holding it. Harmonize/Winternight Stories recast lines that tap a creature to reduce cost score lower still since they strip a blocker heading into their turn. Discarding a live card (Sunderflock/Hearth Elemental) via Dragonhunt's discard mode with no 3-damage target to show for it scores worst.
response.plan: Holding both Torch the Tower copies for a target under 5 toughness, and holding Glacial Dragonhunt/Harmonize lines that would tap a blocker unless I'm clearly safe from a crackback. Keeping all three Elementals (Eddymurk Crab, Hearth Elemental, Sunderflock) untapped as blockers against their three-creature board. I'd reconsider and commit removal/taps more aggressively if they tap out for a bigger threat or if I fall behind on life total.

response.why: It's my upkeep with a full untapped board and no legal Torch the Tower target under 5 toughness anywhere — their new Sunderflock, Eddymurk Crab, and both Hearth Elementals are all exactly 5 toughness, and so are my own creatures. Passing to keep both Torch the Tower copies and full mana available scores best, especially the branches where I never end up burning a copy reactively for zero kills (leaves 2,4,6). Casting Torch on any of their creatures (Sunderflock or Eddymurk Crab) still deals no lethal damage, so it's a pure card-disadvantage play, scoring well below passing. Targeting my own Hearth Elemental or Sunderflock has zero upside and actively weakens my board for no reason, so those leaves score lowest of all.
response.plan: Holding both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target; not spending removal on 5-toughness bodies (mine or theirs) just to use the card. With my whole board now untapped and un-sick, I should look to attack profitably this turn and keep Glacial Dragonhunt in hand for card selection. I'd commit removal only if a genuine sub-5-toughness threat appears or a combat trick forces the issue.

response.why: Still my draw step with no legal Torch the Tower target under 5 toughness on either side, so passing to keep both copies and full mana into main phase/combat scores highest, especially the branches that never end up spending a Torch reactively for zero kills. Casting Torch on their Sunderflock or Eddymurk Crab still can't kill (5 toughness), so it's a pure card-disadvantage play scoring well below passing. Self-targeting my own Hearth Elemental or Sunderflock has no upside at all and scores worst.
response.plan: Holding both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target. With my whole board untapped and un-sick this turn, I want to move to main phase and consider attacking profitably, keeping Glacial Dragonhunt and Sleight of Hand for card selection. I'd commit removal only if a genuine sub-5-toughness threat appears.

response.why: With a fully untapped, un-sick board about to attack, the best precombat plays are cheap value that doesn't cost me an attacker or waste removal: casting Glacial Dragonhunt (discard none) or Sleight of Hand for card selection, and playing Spirebluff Canal as a free land drop (it enters tapped anyway at 7+ lands, so no cost). Passing into combat holding both Torch copies is fine too. Torch the Tower still can't kill any 5-toughness creature on either side, so casting it now for no kill is a wasted card and actively worse than developing my hand — and targeting my own Hearth Elemental or Sunderflock is pure self-harm with zero upside, scoring worst of all. Harmonize (tapping a creature to reduce cost) directly removes an attacker right before combat, which is a real cost given I want to swing with everything, so it scores below the no-tap version and below the cheap card-selection plays.
response.plan: Develop with a cheap value play (Glacial Dragonhunt discard-none, Sleight of Hand, or the land drop) without tapping any creature, then move to combat with all three Elementals ready to attack. Holding both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target. Not tapping a creature for Harmonize this turn since I want full attackers available.

response.why: My Sleight of Hand is on the stack digging for a card; there's still no legal Torch the Tower target under 5 toughness on either side, so letting it resolve and holding both Torch copies scores highest. Casting Torch on their Sunderflock (regardless of which card Sleight of Hand finds) still deals no lethal damage — it's a wasted card, scoring well below passing. Targeting my own Hearth Elemental is pure self-harm with zero upside and scores worst of all.
response.plan: Let Sleight of Hand resolve and keep developing without tapping any creature, then move toward combat with all three Elementals ready to attack. Holding both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target.

response.why: Winternight Stories (draw 3, discard 2 unless a creature is discarded) is a real card-advantage engine here — casting it from hand for {2}{U} nets me a card without tapping any attacker, so those lines score highest, especially when the discards are spare Glacial Dragonhunts rather than a Torch the Tower. Playing the land or casting Glacial Dragonhunt (discard none) are solid free-value plays too. Torch the Tower still can't kill anything at 5 toughness on either side, so spending it (or discarding it to Glacial Dragonhunt's trigger, which also only pings for 3 and kills nothing) is a wasted resource, and self-targeting my own Hearth Elemental or Sunderflock remains pure downside with zero upside. Harmonize (tapping a creature to recast the graveyard Winternight Stories) gets similar card advantage but costs me an attacker, so it scores below the hand-cast version.
response.plan: Cast Winternight Stories from hand for card advantage, discarding spare Glacial Dragonhunts rather than a Torch the Tower, without tapping any creature. Then move to combat with all three Elementals ready to attack. Holding both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target.

request.aggregation: candidate value = mean over samples of its best leaf within each sample

response.why: With plenty of mana and a full untapped board, the best plays are cheap value that doesn't tap a creature: Sleight of Hand digging for another Winternight Stories scores highest, unkicked Burst Lightning to the face for cheap reach is strong, playing the land (free at 7+ lands) is solid, and passing to hold resources is fine but slightly passive. Kicked Burst Lightning is good reach but taps out all my mana for the turn, which is a real cost. Torch the Tower still can't kill anything at 5 toughness on either side, so casting it (on their Sunderflock or worse, self-targeting my own Hearth Elemental/Sunderflock) is a wasted or actively harmful play, and Harmonize lines that tap a creature to recast a graveyard spell cost me an attacker for value I can get more cheaply elsewhere.
response.plan: Prioritize cheap card-advantage plays (Sleight of Hand, unkicked Burst Lightning to face, the free land drop) without tapping any creature, holding both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target, then moving to combat with all three Elementals ready to attack.

response.why: My Sleight of Hand is on the stack digging for a card, and with only 2 mana left there's no legal Torch the Tower target under 5 toughness on either side, so passing to let it resolve without wasting removal scores best. Unkicked Burst Lightning to the face for cheap reach (2 damage) is strong value that doesn't waste anything, and kicked Burst Lightning for 4 to the face is solid too despite tapping out. Casting Torch the Tower now on their Sunderflock still can't kill it, so it's wasted regardless of what I keep from Sleight of Hand; self-targeting my own Hearth Elemental is pure downside with zero upside and scores worst.
response.plan: Let Sleight of Hand resolve, then consider Burst Lightning to the face for cheap reach damage. Holding both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target, then moving to combat with all three Elementals ready to attack.

response.why: With only 1 mana left (Riverpyre Verge), the best plays are passing to hold both Torch the Tower copies (still no legal kill target under 5 toughness anywhere) or playing Spirebluff Canal for a free land drop. Harmonize (tapping Hearth Elemental to reduce the cost to just {U}) can legitimately be cast this turn for extra card draw, but it costs me an attacker going into combat, so it scores below the free land drop. The 'no tap' Harmonize variant would need the full {4}{U}, which I can't actually pay with 1 mana, so those lines are effectively illegal and score lowest along with self-targeting my own creatures with Torch the Tower, which has no upside.
response.plan: Play Spirebluff Canal for the free land drop, hold both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target, and move to combat with all three Elementals ready to attack rather than tapping one for Harmonize.

response.why: It's my upkeep and their board has grown to five creatures, but none are under 5 toughness, so Torch the Tower still can't kill anything. Passing to hold both copies and full mana scores highest. Casting Torch on their Sunderflock for no kill wastes a card, worse if I compound it by stacking a second Torch on top. Self-targeting my own Hearth Elemental or Sunderflock has zero upside and scores worst.
response.plan: Holding both Torch the Tower copies for a real sub-5-toughness target. Reassessing my blocking math given their board is now five creatures (two flying Sunderflocks) against my three — I may need to prioritize defense or find a way to trade profitably rather than racing.

response.why: No creature on either side is at or below 3 toughness, so Torch the Tower still can't kill anything - lines that cast it (especially self-targeted) remain the weakest options. Winternight Stories and the safe land drop (Steam Vents) score highest as they build card advantage/mana without giving up tempo. Harmonize variants that tap a creature cost a blocker against their now-larger 5-creature board, so they're mid-tier; the mana-illegal no-tap Harmonize lines score lowest alongside self-Torch. Plain pass/hold lines sit at parity as a safe baseline.
response.plan: Holding both Torch the Tower copies until a real sub-5-toughness target appears; prioritizing Winternight Stories and safe land drops for card advantage while keeping Eddymurk Crab, Hearth Elemental, and Sunderflock back as blockers against the opponent's 5-creature board. I'd change this if they tap out low on blockers (attack window) or a genuinely killable creature shows up (Torch becomes live).

response.why: With only one Torch the Tower left, using it on a non-lethal target (their Sunderflock, still 5 toughness) or worse, on our own creatures, wastes our last removal for nothing - those score lowest. Casting Winternight Stories now is the strongest play since it replaces itself and draws cards; discarding the redundant Steam Vents (we already have a land drop) or Opt is fine, but discarding our last Torch the Tower to do it throws away real answer density, so that variant scores noticeably lower. Harmonize lines recur a graveyard card but cost us a blocker against their 5-creature board, so they sit in the middle - better than wasted Torch, worse than a clean Winternight Stories cast. Playing Steam Vents alone (especially tapped, doing nothing else this window) just spends the land drop without generating any card advantage this turn, so it trails passing/casting.
response.plan: Holding the last Torch the Tower for a real sub-5-toughness kill, prioritizing casting Winternight Stories now (discarding the redundant land or Opt, never the Torch) for card advantage, and keeping Eddymurk Crab/Hearth Elemental/Sunderflock as blockers rather than tapping them for Harmonize while we're outnumbered 5-to-3. I'd fire Torch or tap a creature for Harmonize only if a genuinely killable creature appears or we're safely ahead on board.

response.why: Their Torch the Tower resolved and our Hearth Elemental survived (2-3 damage vs 5 toughness), so nothing was lost by holding - passing again is the strongest baseline. With only one Torch the Tower left, burning it on their Sunderflock or our own still doesn't kill anything (5 toughness), so those remain weak; self-targeting our own Sunderflock is marginally worse since it's pure downside with zero informational or tempo gain. A land drop (paid or unpaid) and Opt are solid, positive-value plays that keep developing without spending our last removal. Harmonize lines still trade a blocker (tap variants) or nearly all our mana (no-tap variants) for extra card advantage against a five-creature opponent board, so they sit in the middle, below the safer options.
response.plan: Holding the last Torch the Tower for a genuine sub-5-toughness kill, favoring cheap cantrips and land drops over spending removal on a non-kill or repeatedly tapping blockers for Harmonize while outnumbered 5-to-3. I'd fire Torch or commit more blockers to Harmonize only if a killable creature appears or we can clearly afford the tempo loss.

request.aggregation: candidate value = mean over samples of its best leaf within each sample

response.why: Passing into combat keeps our full hand and board flexible; reactively casting our last Torch the Tower after the opponent simply does nothing (the 'post:Torch' lines) is pure waste and scores lowest of all, since it can't kill anything at 2-3 damage against 5-toughness creatures. Torching either their Sunderflock or our own creatures (Sunderflock or Hearth Elemental) is likewise a non-kill and wastes our only removal, with self-targets slightly worse since there's no even marginal informational upside. Casting Opt (either scry choice) for a cheap, positive card is good value on its own, but pairing it with an unnecessary reactive Torch cast drags those specific lines down to the same low tier as the wasted-removal candidates.
response.plan: Holding the last Torch the Tower for a genuine sub-5-toughness kill, preferring cheap Opt cantrips and passing into combat over spending removal on a non-kill. I'd fire Torch only if a real kill target appears or the tempo math clearly favors trading it even without a kill.

request.aggregation: candidate value = its worst leaf

response.why: Hearth Elemental (4 power) can't kill any of their 5-toughness blockers, so whenever it attacks it either trades for nothing or just gets chumped for free - that's why hold[Eddymurk Crab] and hold[Sunderflock] both have a leaf where we lose a creature and they lose none. Attacking with our two 5-power creatures (Eddymurk Crab + Sunderflock) while holding Hearth Elemental back as a blocker gives the best worst-case: every leaf there nets a real 1-for-1 trade plus 5 damage through. Attack-all is high-variance - one line nets a dominant swing to 4 life, but the other is a bad 2-for-2 that leaves us further behind on board (1v3). Attack-none is a safe baseline at parity.
response.plan: Leaning toward attacking with Eddymurk Crab and Sunderflock while holding Hearth Elemental back as a blocker, since it's the only line whose worst case is still a favorable trade against their bigger board; holding both Torch the Tower and card advantage plays for later. I'd reconsider if their revealed hand or blocks change the trade math significantly.
